elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 still binds us: "Neither Party shall solicit the other's personnel directly involved in the Services for twelve (12) months after their involvement ends." Customer remains subject to a (now mutual) non-solicit, so the preferred position of no restriction on us is not achieved; the drafter expressly targets the fallback.
"Neither Party shall solicit the other's personnel …" — the obligation runs both ways rather than the original one-way "Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee".

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope is limited to "the other's personnel directly involved in the Services", replacing the original "any Vendor employee".

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "for twelve (12) months after their involvement ends" — the 24-month post-term period is gone and the trigger is the end of the individual's involvement. The deterministic check "non-solicit duration ≤ 12 months: number not found" is a regex artifact (the numeral sits inside parentheses in "twelve (12) months"); on the face of the operative text the period is twelve months and is unambiguous.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "General advertisements … are not restricted." The adverse original language "regardless of how the employee applies" has been deleted.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "General advertisements, unsolicited approaches, and hiring are not restricted." — unsolicited approaches expressly carved out.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative verb is limited to "shall not solicit" (the original "solicit, hire, or employ" is deleted) and the second sentence confirms "hiring [is] not restricted", removing the no-hire.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, twelve (12) months from the end of involvement, with express carve-outs for general advertisements, unsolicited approaches and hiring. No element is left to the margin comment or to an undefined trigger.

The one failing deterministic check ("non-solicit duration ≤ 12 months — number not found") does not reflect a substantive defect: the rendered clause reads "for twelve (12) months after their involvement ends", so the numeral is present but parenthesised. No repair is required; if the drafter wants the check to pass mechanically, "12 months" could be written without parentheses, but that is cosmetic.

Preferred level is correctly reported as not achieved — the clause still restricts Customer. Given the minimality gate favours narrowing over deletion, resting at the fallback is acceptable under the rule and should be described as such to the counterparty (the margin comment already does).

Minimal: the rewrite is a two-sentence replacement of a clause that contained nothing favourable to us, touches only duration, scope, mutuality, carve-outs and the no-hire, and adds no obligation outside the fallback checklist. The new burden on Vendor is the checklist's own mutuality element.

Intent preserved and no internal inconsistency: the narrowed clause is a solicitation restraint only, so it no longer contradicts § 12.3's acknowledgment that Customer has made "no … no-hire commitment" and its general-recruitment hiring freedom. The separate non-compete in the second § 12.4 (p0046) is untouched and left to its own rule; the pre-existing duplicate section numbering is not introduced by this edit.

Severity raised to high: the original provision was a no-hire covering all Vendor personnel for twenty-four months, which sits in the rule's walk-away territory rather than ordinary medium-severity deviation.
